scenes.title: 3 in 4 prisoners are undertrials
lines: 4,34,302 of 5,73,220 prisoners (75.8%) were undertrials on 31 December 2022
a person in custody is entitled to a free lawyer.
The right exists. The person has to ask for it.
scenes.say: At the end of 2022, three in four of India's prisoners were undertrials. Under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, every person in custody is entitled to a free lawyer. But they have to ask.

scenes.title: Am I entitled? What do I write?
scenes.say: In 2023-24, legal aid reached 15 lakh 50 thousand people, across every group the Act covers. Nyaya Sahayak answers two questions: am I entitled, and what do I write?

scenes.title: Nine yes/no questions
scenes.say: Nine yes or no questions cover every clause of Section 12. Here, a person in custody. Income limits are never hardcoded: each State notifies its own.

scenes.title: The result names the clause
scenes.say: The result names the clause: Section 12, clause g, in custody. Unsure about income? Ask the DLSA, or call the NALSA helpline, one five one, zero zero.

scenes.title: The application, drafted
lines: a request for a panel lawyer
scenes.say: Then it drafts the letter to the District Legal Services Authority, with the facts, the clause, and a request for a panel lawyer. Details never leave the phone.

scenes.title: Documents, Hindi, WhatsApp
scenes.say: It lists the documents to carry. One tap rebuilds the whole letter in Hindi, ready to print, or to send on WhatsApp to a relative or a paralegal.

scenes.title: Every clause is tested
lines: eligibility(answers) is a pure function. 18 tests: every clause, the not-eligible and
don't-know paths, and a test that fails if a rupee amount ever appears in the text.
scenes.say: The rules are a pure function with 18 tests: every clause, the not eligible and don't know paths, and a test that fails if a rupee amount ever appears in the text.
